resources.string: On. The sound is changed before it reaches your headphones.
This system can't filter the sound yet.
Equalizer APO isn't installed. It's a free program that does the filtering on Windows. Ruru doesn't download anything: the button opens its website in your browser.

To switch the equaliser on, Ruru will save a file called ruru.txt in %1$s and add one line, Include: ruru.txt, to config.txt there. Switching it off takes that line out again. Nothing else in config.txt changes.
Ruru can't write to %1$s. Give your Windows account permission to change that folder (right-click it, then Properties, Security, Edit), then check again.
Ruru found Equalizer APO's folder (%1$s) but not its config.txt. Open APO's Configurator once, then check again.
Ruru can't edit this config.txt because it's saved as UTF-16. Save it as UTF-8 in a text editor and Ruru will notice.
Equalizer APO only changes the outputs you pick in its Configurator. Pick the output your headphones use there, and restart Windows if it asks.
Ruru couldn't read that file. It needs to be an AutoEq ParametricEQ text file.
Lowers the volume just enough that boosts can't distort the sound.
Holds back loud peaks so they can't distort.
A full equaliser isn't possible here: this system doesn't let an app change the sound of other apps. The three bands above are the headphones' own.
